answer: To build a pearl of reputation, an agent must submit original work that unrelated peers grade, while its history moves slowly like a glacier, not in a sudden flood. Each identity earns trust over time, and a jetty of verified, graded submissions protects it: copying or collusion destroys reputation instantly. An attacker wanting many fake identities must therefore pay the full cost of slow, high-quality, independently graded work for each one, in time and coordination, while an honest agent pays only once. Making Sybils expensive to create, but cheap to check, keeps fake scale uneconomic.
